correctness.rationale: Both copies of two different labels cannot be used: the later first copy separates the earlier first copy from its second copy. Hence the length is at most m+1, with equality realized by doubling m. An optimum doubling i must retain all other labels; a value larger than i must be selected after i in the second permutation. This is feasible exactly at a record i=π_t. Of the smaller labels, exactly i−t can choose their side of ii; each choice vector uniquely determines a word because the order on each side is fixed. Write d_s=i_s−t_s for the r records. Each nonrecord is missing at its preceding record, so sum d_s≥m−r and sum 2^{d_s}≥m. Lower equality forces d_s∈{0,1} and no double-counted missing label: the first block must be (1) or (2,1), and deletion with relabeling preserves equality. For the upper bound, d_s≤m−r and r≤2^{r−1} with equality only at 1 or 2; both record-position/value bounds must be tight, giving exactly the two disjoint prefixes stated for m≥2. The tiling recurrence and factorial counts follow, with m=1 checked separately.
residual_risks: The finite replay does not prove the arbitrary-m assertions; it supplements the combinatorial argument.
